lesson: Normalize training table [10,20,30] to [0,1], then apply the saved rule to new value 25
audience: Beginners who know subtraction and division; no previous course context assumed.

delivery.canvas: One persistent table, stable row identities and fixed columns; successive states are clicks, not nine slides.
delivery.plannedDuration: Approximately 2-3 minutes, an unmeasured narration budget.
delivery.animation: Only changed values or cells receive attention; scaffolding stays fixed; each operation runs once and holds.
delivery.navigation: Ordinary sequential advance/back in a future implementation; no router or shortcut needed.

branchDecision: No branch is needed: selecting endpoints, subtracting, dividing, and saving the rule fit legibly in the main table. No zoom or artificial focus/return states.

objects.training-table: Persistent rows A=10, B=20, C=30; columns x, x-10, (x-10)/20 begin blank except x.
objects.bounds: Training minimum and maximum annotations attached to rows A and C.
objects.shifted-table: The SAME rows and raw values with the shifted column filled.
objects.normalized-table: The SAME rows with normalized column filled.
objects.saved-rule: Persistent operation strip learned only from training: subtract 10, then divide by 20.
objects.new-row: Separate New row with x=25; training rows and saved-rule remain visible.

conditions: Computed only from training rows A, B, C.
Same training rows in the same order; raw values remain visible.

fixed-rule.statement: For any value x, use y=(x-10)/(30-10)=(x-10)/20 with the established training parameters.
conditions: Training parameters remain minimum=10, maximum=30; do not refit on new data.
For 10<=x<=30, 0<=y<=1; positive training span required. No clipping is introduced.

new-normalized.statement: 25 maps to 15/20=0.75 using the same established rule.
conditions: Use the saved training span 20; training outputs remain [0,0.5,1].

states.purpose: Recognize the training values and the desired 0-to-1 scale.
states.why: These are the data from which we must establish a reusable scale.
states.operation: Static entry: display A=10, B=20, C=30 and target interval [0,1]; output cells empty.
states.visibleResult: Known input is visible; no normalization answers yet.

states.why: To map the smallest training value to 0 and the largest to 1, first locate them.
states.operation: Mark cells A=10 and C=30; attach min=10 and max=30 locally.

states.purpose: Compute the distance between the training endpoints.
states.why: This distance will become one whole unit on the new scale.
states.visibleResult: Training span 20, kept beside the table.

states.purpose: Move the lower endpoint to zero.
states.why: Subtracting the minimum makes 10 become 0 while preserving the row order.
states.operation: Fill the SAME rows: 10-10=0; 20-10=10; 30-10=20. Keep raw column visible.

states.purpose: Make the full training span equal one.
states.why: The shifted maximum is 20, so dividing by 20 maps it to 1.
states.operation: Fill normalized cells from the shifted column: 0/20=0; 10/20=0.5; 20/20=1.
states.visibleResult: Same training rows now map to [0,0.5,1].

states.purpose: Retain the two established operations as a reusable rule.
states.why: New rows must be measured on the same scale as the training rows.
states.operation: Replace only the row-specific input in the operation strip by x: y=(x-10)/(30-10)=(x-10)/20. Label 10 and 20 as fixed from training.
states.visibleResult: Saved rule subtract 10, then divide by 20. Beside it: training span > 0; values within [10,30] map into [0,1].

states.purpose: Introduce a new value on the established scale.
states.why: We can now process a value that was not used to set the scale.
states.operation: Add a separate New row with raw value 25; its shifted and normalized cells are empty. Keep training outputs and saved rule visible.

states.purpose: Apply the first saved operation to 25.
states.why: A position relative to training minimum 10 is needed before dividing by the span.
states.operation: Highlight the saved subtract-10 operation and fill the New row shifted cell with 25-10=15.

states.purpose: Complete the new row using the saved span.
states.why: Dividing by the SAME span 20 places 25 on the SAME 0-to-1 scale.
states.operation: Highlight divide-by-20 and fill 15/20=0.75. Hold the completed table and rule together.
states.visibleResult: Training: 10->0,20->0.5,30->1; New:25->0.75. The rule and training parameters are retained.

retainedConclusion: Training parameters min=10,max=30,span=20 stay fixed; y=(x-10)/20; training [0,0.5,1]; new 25->0.75.
scopeBoundary: The [0,1] guarantee covers the training interval. Values outside it and constant-column handling are not separate lesson topics here.
